what_it_does: AI chips for running neural networks have a limited amount of very fast on-chip memory (think of it as a small scratch pad). As this scratch pad has grown large enough to hold most of a single neural-network layer's data, optimizing just one layer at a time no longer saves much traffic to slow external memory (the large RAM chips outside the chip). SoMa (Scheduling of Memory accesses) tackles the next frontier: fusing multiple layers together and carefully scheduling when the chip fetches data from and writes data back to external memory across those layers. It introduces a new notation — a compact language for describing all the possible schedules — and builds a compiler that searches through those schedules to find one that minimizes expensive memory traffic. This compiler has been deployed on a real commercial chip.
